title: Unpatched Cacti zero-day with public PoC gives remote code execution
content_md: A zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring platform has been publicly disclosed, along with a proof-of-concept exploit that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands on vulnerable servers. The exploit, dubbed " 4HTTP2SHELL " (previously 4HTTP2ROOT), was published on Thanksgiving Day by a cybersecurity researcher known as ek0ms savi0r from the Church of Malware, who demonstrated how the vulnerability can be exploited using just four HTTP requests. Cacti is an open-source network monitoring and graphing tool used to monitor the performance of servers, routers, switches, firewalls, and other network infrastructure. Because the software can store credentials and SNMP passphrases used to access or read data from monitored devices, compromising a Cacti server could potentially give attackers access to other systems on a corporate network. The researcher published a technical write-up, a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, and a video demonstrating the attack in a GitHub repository named "Sad Girls 0day Club." "I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests. No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface," explains the researcher. The vulnerability stems from weak input validation that allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject SQL statements into the application's database and modify commands executed by Cacti's real-time poller.
